mistakes_to_avoid.mistake: Avoid trading D-grade SNIPER signals on low-liquidity altcoins — poor signal quality combined with wide spreads and slippage leads to consistent stop-loss hits
Opening SHORT positions on C-grade signals without strong bearish confirmation — SOL showed upward pressure and the weak signal led to a -3% stop-loss loss.
Avoid LONG entries on low-cap altcoins (like BERA) based solely on 'Extreme Fear reversal' without price confirmation. Extreme fear on small caps often precedes further dumps, not reversals.

Entering LONG on 'trend continuation' without confirming active momentum - if price immediately stalls or reverses after entry with peak PnL < +0.5%, the trend was already exhausted. This is chasing, not trend following.

MISTAKE: Entering LONG based on oversold indicators while orderbook shows persistent sell pressure. FIX: Require orderbook confirmation (neutral or buying pressure) before LONG entry. Oversold + sell pressure = falling knife, not opportunity.

learning_notes.note: Do not execute D-grade signals from SNIPER on low-cap altcoins — the risk/reward is poor and spread costs amplify losses on illiquid pairs
Do not open positions on C-grade signals. A weak signal combined with a SHORT against momentum leads to predictable stop-loss hits. Only trade A/B grade setups.
When a SHORT position reaches +0.6-0.7% profit and orderbook shows BUY_PRESSURE with imbalance >0.6, exit immediately rather than hoping for more - the reversal signal is strong

Oversold reversal + Extreme Fear is a high-probability setup for quick LONG scalps. Set breakeven early at 1.5% and use trailing stops, but when PnL exceeds 5% either take partial profit or use wider trailing to capture extended moves.
At +4% unrealized profit in a volatile asset like XRP, take partial profits (50% position) rather than trailing everything - captured only 33% of peak gain due to tight trailing stop

On oversold reversal setups in Extreme Fear, use wider take profit targets (1.5-2%) since fear reversals often produce sharp moves — this trade showed 1.7% potential but TP was set too conservatively.
Set TP dynamically based on actual price action — when price runs +3.5%, TP should be moved up proportionally. Static TP at +0.2% while having +3.5% unrealized is a configuration error.

Breakeven SL set at 0.1% buffer is too tight for altcoin volatility - got stopped out losing +1.8% unrealized profit. Use minimum 0.5% buffer or set breakeven SL at actual entry price, not 0.1% above.

BERAUSDT showed classic reversal pattern: quick spike to 1.6% then steady decline. For short-duration momentum plays (<15m), implement partial TP at 1.5% threshold or use trailing stop instead of static breakeven.

TP was set too conservatively relative to position momentum. When price reaches +4.9% unrealized, a +1.77% TP captures only 36% of available profit. Consider dynamic TP that scales with trailing stop advancement.

Do not enter 'Extreme Fear reversal' LONG on low-cap altcoins without confirmation. BERA dropped immediately after entry - the fear was justified, not a contrarian opportunity. Wait for actual reversal candle before entering momentum trades.
Do not enter Extreme Fear reversal trades without price confirmation (higher low, bullish divergence, or break of key level). Sentiment is a context, not a trigger.
When SNIPER identifies liquidation cascade, IGNORE RSI overbought/oversold signals and trust trailing stop system — momentum trades can extend far beyond normal RSI boundaries.

Oversold RSI + Extreme Fear reversal is a high-confidence setup for LONG entries. When price validates the thesis (+3% PnL), protect with breakeven SL and let TP run. Fix the duplicate MOVE_SL trigger logic to avoid noise in decision logs.

When trade reaches +1.5% profit and shows signs of reversal (orderbook sell pressure, declining momentum), take partial or full profit rather than waiting for SL to trigger. A 1.6% winner turned into 0.15% breakeven due to excessive patience.
Sniper liquidation cascade SHORT trades should set breakeven early (~0.7%) and use aggressive trailing stops — these moves are fast and reversals are sharp. Lock profits quickly.
When trade reaches +3% profit, set aggressive trailing stop at +1.5% minimum — never let a +3% winner turn into breakeven or loss
Cascade analysis strategy on ETH with 2x leverage and mechanical TP execution produces consistent B+ to A grade results. Entry timing near support with clear TP target is a repeatable setup.

For SHORT entries via sniper_trend_continuation, verify orderbook imbalance is NOT showing buy pressure (imbalance < 0.10 or negative) before entry. A 0.200 buy imbalance should have blocked or delayed this SHORT.

When LONG position shows +0.3-0.4% profit multiple times but SL is never adjusted, eventual stop-out is likely. MUST implement rule: move SL to breakeven once position reaches 0.3% profit with any leverage >= 2x.

Time-based exit rules (Rule 2) conflict with trailing stop strategy - when trailing SL is actively protecting profits and trend is valid, the trailing stop should be the exit mechanism, not arbitrary time limits

SNIPER trend continuation requires CONFIRMED momentum at entry - if price immediately reverses and peak PnL stays below +0.5%, the 'trend' was likely exhausted. Wait for pullback and bounce confirmation before entry.

For profitable SNIPER trades with strong momentum (RSI oversold for SHORT), use trailing stop or dynamic TP instead of fixed TP. A 0.4% exit when 0.6% was available and trend continued means ~33% of potential profit was left on table.
In choppy conditions with weak trend momentum (RSI stuck in narrow range), consider taking partial profit at +0.3-0.4% rather than only moving SL to breakeven, as price may not reach full TP target.
For SNIPER trend continuation shorts, RSI 30 exit is conservative but safe. Consider holding 25-50% of position if momentum is strong and RSI hasn't hit extreme oversold (<25) yet.

Do NOT enter LONG when orderbook shows persistent sell pressure, even if indicators show oversold conditions. Oversold in a downtrend means momentum is bearish - wait for actual price reversal confirmation (higher low, buying volume spike) before entering.

When entering SHORT with RSI already in oversold territory (<30), expect a bounce — either take quick profits at +1% or use wider trailing stops. Tight trailing in oversold conditions leads to premature exits.
When SHORT position shows +0.7% profit with RSI at extreme oversold (<25), immediately take at least 50% profit — do not rely solely on breakeven SL which can get hit on normal retracement

On quick momentum trades, multiple trailing stop adjustments within 1-2 minutes creates a self-fulfilling exit. When profit peaks at 1.3%, either take partial profit or use a fixed trailing distance rather than micro-adjustments that get stopped out on normal retracement.

SNIPER trend_continuation LONG: Do not enter if price immediately reverses after signal — if peak unrealized PnL stays below +0.5% within first 2-3 candles, the trend is exhausted; require pullback to support level and bounce confirmation (green candle closing above pullback high) before entry

SNIPER SHORT: When RSI is oversold (<30) and momentum confirms trend direction, use trailing stop (0.3% trail distance) instead of fixed TP — fixed TP at 0.4% when 0.6%+ was available leaves 30%+ profit on table; trailing stop captures extended moves while protecting gains

SNIPER SHORT: In choppy/ranging conditions (RSI oscillating 40-60 range, ADX <25), take 50% partial profit at +0.3% rather than only moving SL to breakeven — price unlikely to reach full TP in low-momentum environment; secure gains early when trend strength is weak

LONG: Do NOT enter when orderbook shows persistent sell pressure (imbalance < -0.10) even if RSI is oversold (<30) — oversold in a downtrend means bearish momentum continues; require actual price reversal confirmation (higher low on chart + buying volume spike 2x average) before entry

SNIPER SHORT: When RSI is already oversold (<30) at entry, use wider trailing stop distance (0.5-0.6% instead of 0.3%) OR set quick take-profit at +1% — oversold conditions indicate imminent bounce; tight 0.3% trailing gets stopped out prematurely on bounce volatility

SNIPER SHORT: When position shows +0.5-0.7% unrealized profit AND RSI drops to extreme oversold (<25), immediately take 50% partial profit — do not rely solely on breakeven SL; extreme oversold triggers sharp bounces that hit breakeven before resuming trend, losing captured gains

SNIPER: On quick momentum trades (<5 min expected duration), do NOT adjust trailing stop more than once per minute — multiple micro-adjustments within 1-2 minutes create premature exits on normal 0.5-1% retracements; when profit reaches +1.3%, either take 50% partial profit OR set fixed 0.5% trailing distance and stop adjusting

LONG: When unrealized profit reaches +1.5% and orderbook shows increasing sell pressure (bid/ask ratio <0.8) OR momentum indicators decline (RSI dropping from peak, MACD histogram shrinking), take at least 50% partial profit immediately — do not wait for static TP/SL to trigger

SHORT via sniper_trend_continuation: Block entry when orderbook imbalance shows buy pressure (imbalance > 0.10) — a 0.200 buy imbalance indicates buyers are absorbing sells and trend continuation will likely fail
LONG: Move SL to breakeven when position reaches +0.3% profit with leverage >= 2x — repeated unrealized gains of 0.3-0.4% that aren't locked in via SL adjustment lead to eventual stop-out losses

SNIPER trend_continuation LONG: Do not enter if price immediately reverses after signal — if peak unrealized PnL stays below +0.5% within first 2-3 candles, the trend is exhausted; require pullback to support level and bounce confirmation (green candle closing above pullback high) before entry

SNIPER SHORT: When RSI is oversold (<30) and momentum confirms trend direction, use trailing stop (0.3% trail distance) instead of fixed TP — fixed TP at 0.4% when 0.6%+ was available leaves 30%+ profit on table; trailing stop captures extended moves while protecting gains

SNIPER SHORT: In choppy/ranging conditions (RSI oscillating 40-60 range, ADX <25), take 50% partial profit at +0.3% rather than only moving SL to breakeven — price unlikely to reach full TP in low-momentum environment; secure gains early when trend strength is weak

LONG: Do NOT enter when orderbook shows persistent sell pressure (imbalance < -0.10) even if RSI is oversold (<30) — oversold in a downtrend means bearish momentum continues; require actual price reversal confirmation (higher low on chart + buying volume spike 2x average) before entry

SNIPER SHORT: When RSI is already oversold (<30) at entry, use wider trailing stop distance (0.5-0.6% instead of 0.3%) OR set quick take-profit at +1% — oversold conditions indicate imminent bounce; tight 0.3% trailing gets stopped out prematurely on bounce volatility

SNIPER SHORT: When position shows +0.5-0.7% unrealized profit AND RSI drops to extreme oversold (<25), immediately take 50% partial profit — do not rely solely on breakeven SL; extreme oversold triggers sharp bounces that hit breakeven before resuming trend, losing captured gains

SNIPER: On quick momentum trades (<5 min expected duration), do NOT adjust trailing stop more than once per minute — multiple micro-adjustments within 1-2 minutes create premature exits on normal 0.5-1% retracements; when profit reaches +1.3%, either take 50% partial profit OR set fixed 0.5% trailing distance and stop adjusting
